tool_plan.objective: Generate and preserve representative Chrome web-cache content for ChromeCacheView listing, metadata review, preview, and export testing.

required_actions.name: browser.launch
required_actions.why: Launches Chromium to create the browser profile and cache source.

required_actions.name: browser.goto
required_actions.why: Loads distinct documents and resources that can populate the Chrome cache.

required_actions.name: browser.get_clickables
required_actions.why: Observes visible controls and available semantic interactions before exercising them.

required_actions.name: browser.smart_type
required_actions.why: Supplies meaningful search or form input that can produce distinct cached responses.

required_actions.name: browser.smart_click
required_actions.why: Commits visible interactions and follows content links that generate additional cache entries.

required_actions.name: browser.select_option
required_actions.why: Changes observed finite page parameters that can request materially different cached content.

required_actions.name: browser.scroll
required_actions.why: Reveals lazy-loaded or progressive content that may add cached resources.

required_actions.name: browser.close
required_actions.why: Closes Chromium after activity so pending cache data can be flushed for collection.

completion.detail: Complete after Chromium has been closed following representative browsing activity and chromium.cache.cache_data is present for collection.

tool_plan.action_intent_guidance: Action Flow: Launch Chromium, then use browser.goto with relevant run-provided runtime resources when available to load a few varied, content-rich pages that naturally request documents, images, scripts, styles, and media. On interactive pages, use browser.get_clickables to inspect visible controls; perform a bounded observe -> smart_click or select_option -> re-observe loop where relevant controls can load different visible content. Use smart_type only in visible search or form fields and smart_click to submit or follow visible results/content links. Scroll through pages that visibly support progressive or lazy-loaded content, then re-observe controls if new content appears. Visit additional available runtime targets as appropriate, and close Chromium last so cache writes can flush. This activity should populate chromium.cache.cache_data with varied cached responses suitable for listing, metadata review, preview, and export testing. Reason guidance: State the current page/context and the expected cache effect, varying reasons to reflect the action performed, such as loading a resource-rich page, submitting visible search input for a distinct response, selecting a visible content v
